who: Kevin P. Murphy, historian of the United States, gender and sexuality at the University of Minnesota; PhD NYU, 2001.

evidence.says: Minnesota identifies Kevin P. Murphy as professor of history and lists a PhD in United States history from New York University, 2001.
The university reports that Murphy has been a faculty member since 2002, covering the listed supervision years.
The candidate authority is Murphy, Kevin (Kevin Joseph), Ph.D.; its source is Working under the hammer and sickle (2000), identifying a Brandeis University PhD.

notes: Reject p-4158: the candidate is Kevin Joseph Murphy, with a Brandeis doctorate, distinct from Minnesota’s Kevin P. Murphy with an NYU doctorate.

who: Historian of Russia at the University of Illinois Chicago; doctorate Oxford.

who: Joseph Henry Dahmus, professor of medieval history at Penn State; PhD University of Illinois.

who: Laurence W. Dickey, European intellectual historian at Wisconsin–Madison; PhD Berkeley, 1980.

evidence.says: Wisconsin identifies Laurence Dickey as emeritus professor, Berkeley PhD, specialist in European intellectual and social-political theory, and author of Hegel: Religion, Economics, and the Politics of Spirit, 1770–1807.
The CV names Laurence W. Dickey, gives his Berkeley PhD as June 1980, and Wisconsin appointments from 1989, with promotion to professor in 1994.
The authority names Laurence Winant Dickey, with usage Laurence Winant Dickey, III, and cites Hegel (1980) and the published Hegel (1987).

notes: The Hegel work links the authority to the Wisconsin professor. An LC source note gives a conflicting thesis date, 1974; the institutional CV explicitly confirms the AHA’s 1980 degree year.

who: William D. Griffin, historian of Anglo-Irish and modern European history at St. John’s University, New York.

Fordham’s repository identifies William D Griffin as author of The Treason of Marshal Ney: Lons-Le-Saunier, March12-14, 1815 (1959), classified in European and military history.

notes: The authority explicitly supplies the matching history appointment at St. John’s for the supervision period; the Fordham record corroborates his earlier historical scholarship.
